IR.rationale: Trend-followers usually carry long duration positions in a low-rate trending environment, so falling intermediate yields relative to the policy rate mark bond rallies that feed CTA returns.

B.rationale: Easy, trending credit conditions tend to come with persistent risk-asset trends that CTAs ride. The combination isolates a clean easy-credit state.

V.rationale: Time-series momentum has a convex, straddle-like payoff and tends to earn more in high-volatility regimes with large directional moves (crisis alpha).

AP.rationale: Equity index futures are a core CTA holding, so the recent direction of the equity market maps into trend positions and subsequent P&L.

ST.rationale: Strong momentum together with weak short-term reversal indicates persistent price trends rather than choppy mean reversion, the environment in which trend-following earns.

FX.rationale: Broad dollar trends are among the most persistent macro trends and a large share of CTA FX exposure, so the dollar's direction proxies for FX trend profits.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity moves capture trends in energy, metals and agriculture futures that make up a large part of CTA portfolios.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress coincides with sustained deleveraging trends across asset classes, which managed futures have historically monetised.

ENDG.rationale: CTA index returns show some persistence because the underlying trends persist over weeks to months.

IR.rationale: Abrupt rises in intermediate yields signal bond sell-offs against typically long-duration CTA books, raising subsequent P&L variance.

B.rationale: Widening credit spreads signal rising macro risk and cross-asset volatility that passes into futures-based strategies.

V.rationale: Implied volatility forecasts realised volatility beyond its own history. Joint equity and oil volatility signals a broad cross-asset turbulence relevant to diversified futures books.

AP.rationale: Through the leverage and volatility-feedback effect, negative equity returns raise future volatility across risk assets.

ST.rationale: Weak or crashing momentum marks trend turning points, when trend-following positions are wrong-footed and P&L swings widen.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation is a safe-haven and carry-unwind signal associated with risk-off episodes and higher cross-asset volatility.

COM.rationale: Oil sell-offs tend to be accompanied by rising energy volatility, a material component of CTA risk.

MC.rationale: Financial stress indices aggregate funding and market strain and predict higher volatility across asset classes.

ENDG.rationale: When recent variance is elevated relative to history, volatility-targeting de-leveraging and mean reversion shape how much excess variance follows.

IR.rationale: Sudden bond sell-offs reverse the long-duration trend positions common in CTA books and are a classic source of sharp drawdowns.

B.rationale: Widening credit spreads mark regime shifts in risk appetite, which can produce whipsaw losses before new trends establish.

V.rationale: High implied volatility widens the return distribution and raises the probability of tail outcomes for any given position size.

AP.rationale: Equity sell-offs hit CTAs that are long equities after an uptrend, before their signals flip, creating left-tail risk.

ST.rationale: A strong-reversal, weak-momentum regime is the choppy, trend-breaking environment in which trend-followers suffer their largest losses.

FX.rationale: Sharp yen rallies reflect carry unwinds that reverse established FX trends and often hurt CTA positioning.

COM.rationale: Commodity sell-offs often reverse after prior trends and coincide with risk-off rotations that can whipsaw commodity positions.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions signal deleveraging and correlation spikes, which raise the chance of abrupt, simultaneous trend reversals.

ENDG.rationale: After unusually strong recent performance, positions are extended and exposed to trend reversals, which shifts left-tail probability.

IR.rationale: Flight-to-quality bond rallies produce large gains for the long-duration positions typical of trend-followers.

B.rationale: Widening credit spreads mark the sustained risk-off episodes in which managed futures historically deliver crisis alpha.

V.rationale: High market volatility combined with high policy uncertainty signals a macro-driven, directional regime that suits the convex time-series momentum payoff.

AP.rationale: Prolonged equity declines are when CTAs, having turned short, earn their largest right-tail returns.

ST.rationale: Persistent trends with little short-term reversal are the environment that produces outsized trend-following gains.

FX.rationale: Strong dollar trends are among the most persistent macro trends and a frequent source of large CTA gains.

COM.rationale: Persistent commodity downtrends, such as supply-driven bear markets, have been a recurring source of large short-side CTA profits.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress comes with sustained cross-asset deleveraging trends, raising the chance of large CTA gains.

ENDG.rationale: Strong recent returns indicate trends are being captured and tend to persist, raising the probability of a further large gain.
